--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.modularity_matrix()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Get the modularity matrix of the graph. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.modularity_matrix()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Get the modularity matrix of the graph. title: >- [Graph.modularity_matrix()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Get the modularity matrix of the graph. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get the modularity matrix of the graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L93587-L93672){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.modularity_matrix(weighted=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Modularity matrix](../assets/graphs/modularity-matrix.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Two triangles A, B, C and D, E, F joined by the edge C–D, each node badged with its degree, and the 6 by 6 modularity matrix: actual edges minus those expected from the degrees, rounded to one decimal. The positive cells (accent) form one block per triangle plus C–D at 0.4; pairs across the triangles, such as C and E at -0.4, and the diagonal are negative." width="100%"} The modularity matrix compares the actual edges with those expected at random given the degrees: `B = A - k kᵀ / 2m` on an undirected graph, where `k` holds the degrees and `m` is the number of edges (Newman, 2006). Positive entries mark pairs that are more connected than chance. The modularity of a partition is a sum over `B` (see `modularity()`), and its leading eigenvector splits the graph into two communities, the basis of the leading-eigenvector method (`cmty_l_eigenvec()`). On a directed graph this is the Leicht-Newman matrix `A - k_out k_inᵀ / m`. Matches NetworkX's `modularity_matrix()` / `directed_modularity_matrix()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use edge weights. If `None` (default), follows the graph. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [tuple[list[list[float]], list[int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `(matrix, node_ids)`: the matrix as a list of rows, and the node IDs labelling rows and columns, in increasing order. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~modularity_spectrum`) : The eigenvalues of this matrix. [](`~modularity`) : The modularity of a partition, a sum over this matrix. [](`~cmty_l_eigenvec`) : Communities from this matrix's leading eigenvector. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Every row of the undirected modularity matrix sums to zero: ::: {#67b1e7c3 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec import polars as pl path = ec.Graph.from_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D")]) matrix, nodes = path.modularity_matrix() labels = [path.get_label_from_id(n) for n in nodes] pl.DataFrame( [[round(v, 3) + 0.0 for v in row] for row in matrix], schema=labels, orient="row", ).insert_column(0, pl.Series("node", labels)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}
shape: (4, 5)
nodeABCD
strf64f64f64f64
"A"-0.1670.667-0.333-0.167
"B"0.667-0.6670.333-0.333
"C"-0.3330.333-0.6670.667
"D"-0.167-0.3330.667-0.167
``` ::: ::: ### Scoring the split `karate_club()` links the 34 members of a university karate club who met outside the club, before it split in two. Adding up the matrix over the pairs of members on the same side, and dividing by twice the number of friendships, gives the modularity of the split, as `modularity()` computes it: ::: {#61cf6895 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} karate = ec.karate_club() faction = karate.get_node_attrs("faction") b, nodes = karate.modularity_matrix() same = sum( b[i][j] for i, u in enumerate(nodes) for j, v in enumerate(nodes) if faction[u] == faction[v] ) sides = [{n for n in nodes if faction[n] == f} for f in (1, 2)] round(same / (2 * karate.count_edges()), 4), round( karate.modularity(sides), 4 ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (0.3715, 0.3715) ``` ::: ::: ::: {#09614359 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} karate.plot(color_by="faction", label_by="label", seed=1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
